Geely Auto Group: Building Certified AI Safety into Vehicle Development  October 16, 2026 Geely Auto Group has become the first global automaker to achieve ISO/PAS 8800 certification for its AI safety engineering processes, following independent evaluation by SGS-TÜV. The certification confirms that Geely's defined development capability - spanning functional safety, expected functional safety and AI safety - meets the requirements of three converging international standards, as intelligence becomes increasingly central to vehicle value. About Geely Auto Group Geely Auto Group is a leading automobile manufacturer headquartered in Hangzhou, China. Founded in 1997 as a subsidiary of Zhejiang Geely Holding Group, the Group manages several major brands, including Geely Auto, Lynk & Co and Zeekr, and is the global strategic partner of Malaysian national automaker PROTON. A new standard, and the challenge of catching up fast As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly central to vehicle value and brand differentiation, Geely set out to build a systematic capability for the safe application of AI in its vehicles, aligned with the newly published ISO/PAS 8800. Geely had already established functional safety processes under ISO 26262 and SOTIF processes under ISO 21448 at concept and system level, with these processes certified by UL. Building on this foundation, Geely moved into the software phase and expanded into AI safety in line with ISO 8800:2024, developing new processes and seeking third-party certification to catch up quickly with the latest standard. Closing the gap: how we supported the certification journey We carried out a gap analysis of Geely's development processes against the requirements of ISO/PAS 8800, delivered by two experts at SGS-TÜV Saar in Germany.
